text:
The defendant will be found not guilty of arson. Common-law arson requires malice, meaning intent or reckless disregard of a known risk of fire, and his forgetting to turn off the stove was at most ordinary negligence. Voluntary intoxication can't supply the missing mental state, so the charge fails for lack of mens rea. The note's "felony grade" rationale is not why: arson is defined by the malicious burning of a dwelling, not by whether the defendant committed some other felony.

CONFIDENCE: 82
